How this was checked: I read the diff in full context and confirmed it equals the commit's change to build_site.py. No test ran and no site was built. I did call the old and new converter functions in memory from my scratchpad, on the 665 pages site.pages expands to, and wrote nothing to the worktree.

Does the new break in _list end a list where GitHub would continue it? Only in one case nothing reaches, finding 3.
- An indented heading or quote is taken by the earlier indent > base branch, so it behaves as before.
- A column-0 '>', '---', '***' or '___' after an item ends the list on GitHub too: a quote interrupts a paragraph, and a rule is not a lazy line.
- '#hashtag' has no space after the marks, so it stays a lazy continuation.
- Across the 665 pages exactly one list item is directly followed by a heading, fence, quote or rule at any indent: theories/LINEAGE.zh.md:150. The old and new HTML differ on that page alone, and only by dropping ' ## 改名' from the list's last item and adding its h2.

why:
The finding holds. I checked it against the raw ar5iv text of arXiv:2310.13548; the latest PDF's text could not be extracted here.

What the paper says: Section 4.2 reads "We use the Claude 2 PM, which was trained on a mix of human preference judgments and AI preference judgments (Anthropic 2023). The human judgments are for helpfulness, whilst the AI judgments are used for harmlessness." It then optimizes against that PM by best-of-N and tracks "the reinforcement learning (RL) phase of Claude 2 finetuning". Section 4.3.2 also uses this PM and variants of it. "Constitution" appears only in the bibliography entry for Bai et al. 2022b, and that paper is cited only in section 2, as a general remark on AI-generated preference judgments. So the finding's caveat is right: the paper does not say these AI judgments read written principles.

Why item 3 is wrong: USES-EXAMPLES item 3 says none of the three measurements was on this pipeline and that "they measured pipelines trained on human preference". The refutation I tried was that Sharma's five assistants (section 3) and the hh-rlhf analysis (section 4.1) are human feedback. That is true, but 07 §6 cites the measurement for "optimizing through it", and the only optimizing in Sharma is the PM work in 4.2 and 4.3.2. The study's own sentence, "Optimizing against preference models sometimes traded truthfulness for agreement", comes from there. That PM has the same human-helpfulness, AI-harmlessness split the audit itself describes for this pipeline, so the contrast fails on the very respect the sentence draws it. The flag "figures read from the papers' abstracts" covers figures, not this flat description of what was measured. Filing Sharma under the study's section 1 heading, "Reward models trained on human preference (RLHF)", carries the same error, and item 3 links that section as its support. The Sharma bullet's own sentences are not false; they are silent on the split and misfiled.

Severity: medium, at its lower end. It misdescribes a cited paper in a categorical negative on a reader-facing page, and a specialist would catch it. It understates rather than overstates the evidence, and no law or standing changes: T3 stays conjectured and the bearing stays a reading.

Limits the fix should keep:
- "Of this kind" holds only for the split, not for written principles.
- The PM is "trained in part using the data analyzed in §4.1", and the paper does not separate which half drives sycophancy, so the AI half is not shown to matter.
- Section 4.2 reports "mixed effects": best-of-N reduces answer and mimicry sycophancy, and RL increases some forms, so "sometimes" should stay.
- Gao should keep the page's existing clause about a gold reward model standing in for the humans, rather than being called simply trained on human preference.
- The English and Chinese fronts' "Beside published measurements" paragraphs and 07 §6 do not make the false contrast. A grep of the Chinese edition for the audit's terms found no matching item, so it may not carry this audit at all.
- The record's history should gain a line, as with the 8 November section 2 correction.
